Ah, if you completely wiped out the `android/build` directory, you need to make sure there's a `.gdignore` file in there.

Now that some extra stuff has snuck in there, you may need to completely wipe out the `android/build` directory again, but after you unzip the `android_source.zip`, create an empty file called `.gdignore` in `android/build` as well.

Otherwise, the Godot editor will create `.import` files for each of the resources it finds, and that will make Gradle unhappy.

> Thank you for sharing a smaller version of the template ^^ but it's weird it's like I have the import error each time even with the .gdignore file...

You shouldn't have the error with the `.gdignore` file so long as you add it before the editor runs its import process.

Unless you change the configuration, Godot will only import when the editor window is focused, so I can usually get away it by making sure I don't focus the window before adding the file. If you have configured Godot to import even when the window is unfocused, then it's a race between you and Godot :-)

At minimum, you should build it yourself, so that you are in control of the code and build options. Who knows what options I used to build it - not even me anymore, it was just something I threw together in a couple minutes. :-) Or, you can wait a few days and use an official release, which will be built in the same way all official builds are done.
